primaryQuery: red centre way camping (alice springs, kings canyon, uluru)
accuracyFlags: 'The water in these gorges is snowmelt-cold year round': wrong. There is no snowmelt in Central Australia; gorge waterholes are cold from permanent shade and groundwater.

'Both ranges have basic national park campgrounds requiring a Parks and Wildlife pass' / 'NT parks pass required': the NT has no general parks pass; campground fees are paid per site (booked via NT Parks), and entry to Uluru-Kata Tjuta needs the separate Commonwealth pass (not mentioned, a big omission on an Uluru route).

Mereenie Loop 'permit is inexpensive': sources quote roughly $5-$6.50 per vehicle for 3 days, undated; state the figure and the official source (Central Land Council / Discover Central Australia). Check whether any section has been sealed before saying 'unsealed'.
Kings Canyon Rim Walk heat closure and 'four litres of water per person' stated with no NT Parks source; Larapinta 223 km is correct.
'Updated 18 August 2026' but nothing on the page is dated or sourced to 2026.
